title: mos.drive.v1
description: Static drive facts emitted by `mos drive --json`: what IS this drive, vs mos.metadata.v1's what disc is this (design: doc/research/2026-06-10-media-info-design.md and 2026-06-16-drive-identity-enrichment-survey.md). This is the verb where the user asks for the canonical truth, so identity (vendor/product/firmware), version and version_descriptors are read FRESH from a raw standard INQUIRY, with the DiscRecording directory cache as fallback; protection/profiles/firmware_date are one GET CONFIGURATION RT=0 walk. The drive-disc JOIN is consumer-side: the pipeline that loaded a disc knows which drive it used. serial is the durable inventory key that survives replug and machine moves; registry_id is ATTACHMENT identity (replug mints a new one) and must not be used as a durable key.

bsd_node.description: Whole-disk dev node of the current media, or null when the drive is empty. Addressing context — a drive property only while this disc is loaded.

registry_id.description: Drive service IORegistry entry ID — attachment identity, the state/event join key. 0 = unavailable. NOT durable: replug mints a new ID by construction.

vendor.description: Friendly vendor name (mos_vendor_friendly_name) when mos maps the raw SCSI string to a community name (e.g. "LG"); otherwise the raw INQUIRY vendor string. FRESH from this verb's raw standard INQUIRY, falling back to the DR cache when the raw read can't run (BUSY/mounted); null when neither has it. Same sanitization rules as mos.state.v1.

vendor_oem.description: Raw SCSI INQUIRY vendor string (SPC-4 §6.4.2 bytes 8-15, trailing-space trimmed). Same source/sanitization/fallback rules as vendor. null when vendor is null.

product.description: Product identification, same terms/source as vendor.

revision.description: Firmware revision (SPC-4 PRODUCT_REVISION_LEVEL) — the firmware VERSION (4 chars); the creation date is firmware_date. Same terms/source as vendor (fresh INQUIRY, DR fallback).

serial.description: Drive serial — the durable drive-inventory key that survives replug and machine moves (registry_id is attachment identity, replug mints a new one). Read from the Logical Unit Serial Number feature (0108h) in the non-exclusive GET CONFIGURATION walk: no raw command and no exclusive access, so it is read even while a disc is mounted (design: AGENTS.md serial-source ADR). null when the drive does not implement the feature or programs no serial — it is OPTIONAL in MMC and population is firmware-dependent. (VPD page 0x80, the SPC/block-storage serial carrier, is NOT used: wrong abstraction for an MMC drive, and empirically empty on the optical drives surveyed.)

interconnect.description: Physical bus the drive attaches over, from the DiscRecording directory (kDRDevicePhysicalInterconnectKey) — zero commands, read at open. Internal SATA/PATA optical reports "atapi" (the DR value covers ATA/ATAPI); an external enclosure reports "usb" or "firewire". null when DR does not report the key. Closed enum: an unrecognized DR value reads as null, never a new token. (Whether DR populates the key for a given USB-SATA bridge is hardware-falsifiable per the hardware-role ADR; null degrades cleanly.)

interconnect_location.description: Whether the drive is internal or external (kDRDevicePhysicalInterconnectLocationKey), from the same zero-command DR read. "unknown" is the DR-reported value Unknown; null means DR omitted the key entirely. Closed enum.

protection.description: Copy/content-protection schemes the drive CAN authenticate, from the GET CONFIGURATION feature list — a drive CAPABILITY, not per-disc state (the per-feature Current bit, media-dependent, is ignored) and not enforcement (region/key state lives behind REPORT KEY, which mos does not issue — scope doctrine). A modern BD drive advertises AACS+CSS at minimum, so the set reads as the schemes this drive speaks. Spec-grounded bits only — the same a MakeMKV drive dump shows as 'Highest AACS version' / bus-encryption flags, WITHOUT the LibreDrive status synthesis (a MakeMKV database property, not a drive property; mos emits no libredrive field by design). Version-carrying schemes (aacs/css/cprm) are an object when present and null when absent; presence-only schemes (securdisc/vcps) are a boolean.

aacs.description: AACS feature (010Dh): object when the drive advertises AACS (BD units), null otherwise (every non-BD drive — data, not an error).

bus_encryption.description: DRIVE-REPORTED bus-encryption (read) support — AACS BEC bit (feature payload byte 0 bit 1, per libaacs/UDFclient agreement). A firmware assertion: the cryptographically signed BEC bit lives in the AACS drive certificate behind REPORT KEY, which mos does not issue (scope doctrine).

write_bus_encryption.description: DRIVE-REPORTED write-bus-encryption support — AACS WBE bit (feature payload byte 0 bit 2): the drive can write sectors subject to bus encryption (WBE=0 = bus encryption only drive→host). JSON-only; the human Protection row omits it.

css.description: DVD CSS/CPPM feature (0106h): object when present, null otherwise.

cprm.description: DVD CPRM feature (010Bh): object when present, null otherwise.

securdisc.description: SecurDisc feature (0113h) present — presence-only (Additional Length 0, no version).

vcps.description: VCPS feature (0110h) present — legacy (MMC-5), presence-only (no version).

write_protect.description: Write Protect Feature (0004h) CAPABILITY bits, from the same RT=0 GET CONFIGURATION walk (MMC-6 §5.3.5, Table 101). This is what the drive can REPORT/CHANGE about write protection — NOT whether the loaded disc IS write-protected (that is the Timeout & Protect mode page 1Dh / MECHANISM STATUS, which mos does not read). An object when the feature is present, null when absent. Closed field set.

software_write_protect.description: Drive supports the SWPP (Software Write Protect Until Power-down) bit of the Timeout & Protect mode page.

persistent_write_protect.description: Drive supports set/release of Persistent Write Protect (PWP) status.

write_inhibit_dcb.description: Drive supports writing the Write Inhibit DCB on DVD+RW media (READ/SEND DISC STRUCTURE format 30h, Media Type 0).

disc_write_protect.description: Drive supports reading/writing the Disc Write Protect PAC on BD-R/-RE media (READ/SEND DISC STRUCTURE format 30h, Media Type 1).

capabilities.description: Curated presence flags for optional MMC features in the RT=0 GET CONFIGURATION walk — the named subset `mos drive` surfaces (the same walk `mos features` dumps raw). Each is the presence of the feature descriptor; no further payload is decoded. Always present (false when the feature is absent), unlike protection/write_protect which null out.

real_time_streaming.description: Real-Time Streaming feature (0107h) — host-paced read/write performance (SET/GET PERFORMANCE, stream recording).

power_management.description: Power Management feature (0100h) — host/drive power management support.

timeout.description: Time-out feature (0105h) — drive responds to commands within a bounded time.

profiles.description: Supported-profile set from the GET CONFIGURATION Profile List feature (0x0000) — the drive-static disc types this drive handles (the modern, BD-aware capability set, superseding the legacy MODE SENSE page-0x2A read/write media bits). The per-descriptor Current bit is media-dependent and deliberately omitted; this is what the drive CAN do, irrespective of the loaded disc. Empty array when the feature was absent (data, not an error). A consumer matches a profile by its stable MMC code or its name; an unknown code carries name null and is identified by code.

code.description: MMC profile number as lowercase hex (e.g. 0x0008 CD-ROM, 0x0010 DVD-ROM, 0x002b DVD+R DL, 0x0043 BD-RE).

name.description: Lowercase profile name (mos_profile_name), or null for a code mos does not name (consumer falls back to code).

version.description: Standard INQUIRY VERSION byte (SPC compliance level), from a raw standard INQUIRY (EVPD=0). null when that read could not be performed (BUSY / mounted media) — the same exclusive-access self-gating as serial.

name.description: SPC-level token (mos_spc_version_name): spc / spc_2 … spc_5; null for 0 (none), legacy SCSI-1/2, or unknown (consumer uses code).

version_descriptors.description: The T10/ISO standards the drive claims, from the INQUIRY version descriptors (bytes 58-73 of standard INQUIRY data). Empty array when the standard INQUIRY was unreadable (BUSY) or the drive listed none. Each code is the stable 2-byte descriptor value; a consumer matches by code or name.

code.description: Version descriptor code, lowercase hex (e.g. 0x04e0 MMC-6, 0x0460 SPC-4).

name.description: Standard token (mos_version_descriptor_name) for the 'no version claimed' family codes; null for a specific-revision or non-listed code (consumer uses the hex code).

firmware_date.description: Firmware creation timestamp from the GET CONFIGURATION Firmware Information feature (010Ch; MMC-6 §5.3.43 Table 197 — Century/Year/Month/Day/Hour/Minute/Second decimal ASCII, GMT), on the same RT=0 walk that yields protection/profiles. SAME RFC 3339 UTC format as mos.event.v1's `ts` (integer seconds, trailing Z). null when the drive does not implement the feature (common). NOTE: this is the firmware's CREATION date, not a version string — the `revision` field (4-char PRODUCT_REVISION_LEVEL) is the version identifier.

mechanical.description: MODE SENSE(10) page 0x2A (MM Capabilities & Mechanical Status) via the ModeSense10 convenience method — the mechanical facts GET CONFIGURATION cannot carry: loading-mechanism type, eject/lock support, the live media-locked bit, the drive buffer size, and the read/rip capability bits (BURN-Free, multisession, accurate CD-DA stream, C2 error pointers). Read-only (no MODE SELECT). null when the command failed or page 0x2A was absent. loading_mechanism and eject are kernel-confirmed (sr.c get_capabilities); buffer_kb, the lock bits, and the rip-cap bits are the standard MMC-3 page-2A positions with no in-repo capture yet (hardware falsifier per the ADR).

loading_mechanism.description: Loading-mechanism token (page[6] bits 7:5 via mos_loading_mechanism_name), or null for a reserved/unknown code.

locked.description: Media is currently locked (page[6] bit 2) — the live state bit.

burn_free.description: Drive supports buffer-underrun-free recording / BURN-Free (page[4] bit 7, BUF).

multisession.description: Drive can read multisession media — sessions > 1 (page[4] bit 6).

accurate_stream.description: Drive's CD-DA read stream is accurate (page[5] bit 1) — an EAC/AccurateRip-relevant capability.

c2_pointers.description: Drive reports C2 error pointers (page[5] bit 4) — EAC/AccurateRip-relevant. NOTE: a claim of support, not a guarantee of accuracy; C2 reliability is firmware-dependent.

error_recovery.description: MODE SENSE(10) page 0x01 (Read/Write Error Recovery) via the ModeSense10 convenience method — the drive's read error-recovery configuration. Read-only: mos reports it, it never issues the MODE SELECT that recovery tools (dvdisaster, sdparm) use to tune it. null when the command failed or page 0x01 was absent.
